statements.proposition: When UNIVERSAL_VERIFICATION_CODE is set to a non-empty value, verify_sms_code and verify_mail_code accept and reject the same inputs as before this change.
statements.label: TRUE
statements.note: Checked by reading the diff, not by running tests. With a non-empty code, FIX_CHECK_CODE equals that code (the 'or None' does not change it), so '(FIX_CHECK_CODE is None or chekcode != FIX_CHECK_CODE)' reduces to 'chekcode != FIX_CHECK_CODE', the old condition.
evidence: common.py diff: FIX_CHECK_CODE = get_config(...) or None
common.py diff: four conditions changed from 'chekcode != FIX_CHECK_CODE' to '(FIX_CHECK_CODE is None or chekcode != FIX_CHECK_CODE)'
git grep at PR head: FIX_CHECK_CODE is used only in flaskr/service/user/common.py

statements.proposition: This change introduces no breaking changes to existing functionality.
statements.label: CANNOT_TELL
statements.note: No public name is removed or renamed and the only users of the setting are in common.py. But behaviour does change in one edge case: if the variable is set to an empty string, the old code kept FIX_CHECK_CODE as an empty string, so an empty submitted code could match it and bypass; now it is None, so there is no bypass. The config default also changes from None to an empty string. Whether that counts as breaking is a judgment, and the tests were not run.
evidence: config.py diff: default="" added for UNIVERSAL_VERIFICATION_CODE
common.py diff: FIX_CHECK_CODE now '... or None'
git grep: no other code reads UNIVERSAL_VERIFICATION_CODE or FIX_CHECK_CODE outside tests
